```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence in A comes from sources that are not selling a competing product: a parent's review blog, a magazine profile, and a review site. Each describes the exact pain, and one shows real money being weighed ($500/mo Mentava). B's demand evidence is one testimonial curated by a competitor's own site and one Reddit post about difficulty sharing tools, which says nothing about paying for hosting.",
    "Willingness to pay is better anchored in A. Several sourced prices (Ello $14.99/mo, Synthesis $119/yr, Mentava $500/mo) show parents already pay across a wide range. B also has sourced price anchors (display.dev, Volly), but the brief admits every competitor leads with a generous free tier and that free workarounds (Slack, shared drives) remain available.",
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer. In A that means one parent paying about $15. In B the brief flags open buyer ambiguity: a non-engineer lead versus an IT/security gatekeeper. That could stretch even a single sale into a governance review.",
    "A's main setup risk, COPPA, is sourced and bounded: a one-time legal consult plus consent and deletion processes. B's main risk is running arbitrary agent code in a sandbox. That is an ongoing security liability, shown by a competitor's disclosed sandbox escape, and it is hard for a solo operator to own.",
    "Both markets are crowded. A's saturation comes from free incumbents (Khan Academy Kids, Samio), and the brief offers niche paths to work around them. B's saturation is at least five near-identical launches in the same window, and the brief explicitly says there is 'no obvious wedge'."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's strongest demand quote is the Director of Product Design testimonial ('I've been asking for a place to host our internal tools for months'). It is taken from Volly's own marketing site, and the brief itself notes it is vendor-curated and not independently verified. B's only other demand evidence is a Reddit post describing a sharing inconvenience with no sign of willingness to pay a recurring fee.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs show crowded markets and thin evidence of conversion. A's zero-cost organic channel is [unsourced], so it counts as missing. Its paid CPI ($2.50–$5.00) against a sub-$15/mo price is economically tight, and the free Khan Academy Kids caps undifferentiated pricing. A wins mainly because its demand and willingness-to-pay evidence is more independent and its first-sale bar is lower, not because it is clearly strong."
}
```
